title: Real-time LLM tasks: a slow coding agent that builds, monitors and repairs fast controllers

verification_legend.S: secondary source or search snippet only

pitch.yoav: Frontier LLM agents can now discover the rules of an unfamiliar game and write a solver (our AVO PuzzleScript work), but they take seconds to minutes per decision, so they cannot act inside anything that runs on a clock. The thesis asks how a slow language agent should spend its reasoning when the world will not wait. Proposed answer: the agent compiles what it learns into fast artifacts (code controllers, typed System One decision calls such as Jev and the open JEV-27B-VL, which is built on the same Qwen 3.8-27B backbone as our small-model thread, and optionally a distilled policy) and returns to the loop only when the fast layer reports low confidence, a prediction mismatch or novelty. This extends AVO solver evolution to online, time-pressured operation, with clean metrics: score vs wall-clock, latency percentiles, LLM calls per minute and escalation precision. The nearest 2026 work (Code to Control) synthesises reactive controllers offline but does not repair them while the clock runs or learn unknown rules.
pitch.gal: A modern deliberative/reactive hybrid architecture in which the deliberative layer is an LLM coding agent that writes the behaviours the reactive layer executes, and is called back by a monitor when execution departs from expectation. The escalation trigger is close to socially attentive monitoring and plan recognition (Kaminka & Tambe, JAIR 2000): it fires when expected and observed behaviour diverge, for the agent itself or for teammates. The natural testbed is RoboCup Soccer Simulation 2D (rcssserver, 100 ms cycles, 11 decentralised players), where his group did foundational teamwork work with ISIS (RoboCup-97), and where we found no published LLM work. The questions: can a coding agent act as an online coach that writes, tests and repairs team behaviours during a match, and can teamwork monitoring decide when that slow coach must intervene? A lighter swarm variant (VMAS) connects to his current swarm and modular-RL work.

framework.name: Coder-Controller loop

components.name: Slow coding agent
components.role: Existing harness (Codex/Claude Code/OpenCode/Antigravity); learns rules, writes/repairs controllers; asynchronous, never on the tick path

components.name: Learned world model
components.role: Rules as code; feeds controller predictions and the monitor

components.name: Controller library
components.role: Python controllers with precondition/act/predict, tests, metadata; typed decision questions as tested library items

components.name: Test bench
components.role: Replay traces + world-model rollouts; engine fork via checkpoint/restore as oracle ablation

components.name: Arbiter
components.role: Every tick: select controller, enforce deadline, fallback/safe action, commit action chunks (RTC idea)

components.name: Decision service
components.role: decide(state, questions) -> answer, probs, confidence; backends: Jev API, JEV-9B / JEV-27B-VL, typed small LLM

components.name: Optional learned policy
components.role: Behaviour cloning from controller and paused-LLM traces

components.name: Monitor + escalation
components.role: Triggers: exception/overrun, no applicable controller, prediction mismatch, low confidence, novelty, stall; rate-limited async queue to the agent

components.name: Logging
components.role: Tick log, decision calls, escalations, controller versions

latency_budget.budget: p99 < tick period when synchronous; else async with committed chunk

metrics: fraction of ticks under code control
baselines: B0 paused LLM every step (upper bound)
B1 LLM every step in real time
B2 frozen fast-only controllers (Code to Control-like)
framework.first_experiment: Two weeks, PuzzleScript only. Week 1: audit the 7 games excluded only for realtime (Sneeze, Beam Islands, Boxes & Balloons, Magik, Oskar's Maze, Pushcat Jr, Some Lines) for genuine time pressure and pick 3-4; add a TICK no-op action and a clock driver (tick every realtime_interval x slowdown); build a minimal arbiter (hot-reloaded controllers, deadline + fallback, monitor, file-queue escalation) and a tick log. Week 2: one frontier harness; per game x slowdown {8,4,1} x 2 seeds run B0 paused LLM, B1 real-time LLM every step, C1 Coder-Controller with code controllers only, C2 = C1 + one typed tactical question via Jev or self-hosted JEV-9B. Deliverable: levels solved vs slowdown per condition, a latency/calls/escalation table, and five annotated escalation-repair episodes. Hypothesis: B1 collapses as slowdown -> 1 while C1/C2 stay near B0 at a fraction of its LLM calls per minute.
